If the weights are split into k k approximately equal blocks, then the method guarantees an ( ε , δ ) (\varepsilon,\delta) -budget with a total of k ⋅ T k\cdot T steps, where T T is the number of steps for the baseline algorithm without decomposition. These steps are computationally lighter, and in practice, the total can be smaller than k ⋅ T k\cdot T . As in the original noisy fine-tuning method, we add several standard fine-tuning steps after unlearning. Thus, for small T T , the overall runtime is close to that of the baseline, while the block-wise method achieves better and more stable accuracy.
